title: Challenge: Knowing Yourself
rule: My life is bigger than my current situation.

days.task: Write 3 things you are grateful for today. They can be big or small things that made your day better.
days.example:
I am grateful for the food I ate today.
I am grateful that my friend made me laugh.
I am grateful that I have a phone to learn from.

days.task:
Watch a YouTube video about a successful person who started with very little. Write one thing you learned from their story.
Suggested people: Dhirubhai Ambani, Rajinikanth, Karsanbhai Patel, Sundar Pichai, APJ Abdul Kalam
days.example: I watched Dhirubhai Ambani's story. I learned that where you start does not decide where you can reach.

days.task: Find one problem in your home, neighbourhood, or area that you would like to help solve someday.
days.example: There is no dustbin near our school gate, so people throw wrappers on the road. I think I could help by asking for a dustbin or organising a clean-up.

days.task:
Make your Support Group.
Write the names of 5 people who are helpful, caring, and support others. They can be family members, friends, teachers, or neighbours.
days.example: My mother, my friend Arjun, my class teacher, my neighbour uncle, and my cousin.

days.task: Think of one person around you whom you respect and admire. This person can be someone you see regularly and learn from by observing them.
days.example: A woman in my neighbourhood runs a small tiffin service from home. I admire her hard work and self-reliance.

days.task:
Answer these two questions honestly:
-What is the biggest problem in your life right now?
-What is one problem your family faces that you wish you could solve?
There is no right or wrong answer.
days.example: My biggest problem is that I get distracted easily and cannot study for long. My family's problem is financial stress, and I want to help them in the future.

title: Challenge: Self-Introspection
rule: I will find my strengths and use them to build my life.

days.task:
What are your main strengths and weaknesses?
Choose from the list below or write your own.
Strengths:
Good listener, Creative, Hardworking, Caring, Quick learner, Good at sports, Strong memory, Natural leader, Good with numbers, Good communicator, Calm under pressure, Energetic, Organised
Weaknesses:
Gets distracted easily, Overthinks, Procrastinates, Loses confidence quickly, Avoids difficult conversations, Impatient, Forgets responsibilities, Struggles to focus
days.example: My strengths are that I am a good listener and very caring. My weaknesses are that I overthink and procrastinate.

days.task:
Think about something you can do naturally, without training, that other people find difficult. 
If you are not sure, ask a parent or close friend what they think you are naturally good at.
days.example: I can explain things in a simple way. My friends often ask me to explain lessons because they understand me easily.

days.task:
What is something you are excited to achieve or build in the future?
It could be a career, skill, goal, or mission. If you are not sure, write the closest thing that comes to your mind.
days.example: I want to become very good at communication and public speaking because I have ideas but sometimes struggle to express them.

days.task:
Look at the 5 people in your support group from Week 1.
Think about your goal from Day 3. Write how each person could help you move closer to that goal.
days.example: My mother can remind me to stay consistent. My teacher can guide me in my studies. My cousin can share advice from college. My friend Arjun can study with me.

days.task:
Think about the local role model you chose in Week 1.
What challenges did they face? How did they deal with those challenges? What helped them keep going?
days.example: The woman who runs a tiffin service in my neighbourhood did not get much support at first. But she kept working hard and never gave up. I learned that you do not need perfect conditions to start.

days.task:
What is your dream?
Then write how you plan to start working towards it. Your plan does not need to be perfect. Just write the most honest plan you can think of right now.
days.example: My dream is to become a civil engineer and help build affordable homes. My plan is to focus on Maths and Science, learn about engineering colleges and talk to people in the field.

title: Challenge: Identity Shift
rule: I shall build the right inspiration to build myself.

days.task:
Choose one global role model who inspires you. This can be someone in your future career or someone whose life you admire.
Research them and write:
3 habits they follow
3 qualities they have
1 problem they solved that made them successful
days.example: I chose APJ Abdul Kalam. He woke up early, read regularly, and worked hard throughout his life. He was humble, disciplined, and cared about young people. He helped develop India's missile programme when the country had limited technology.

days.task: Write 5 reasons why you chose this role model.
days.example:
He came from a small town.
He had very little money growing up.
He never blamed his background.
He stayed humble.
He believed in young people.

days.task:
Look at your support group and local role model from Week 1.
Write one quality in each person that helps them succeed or will help them succeed. Also write why.
days.example:
My mother never gives up, even in difficult times.
My teacher prepares for every class, even after many years of teaching.
My local role model works consistently every day without excuses.

days.task:
Think about 3 habits in your daily life that need to change.
Be honest. No one is judging you.
You can think about:
Laziness, Time management, Phone usage, Study habits, Forgetting responsibilities, Helping at home
days.example:
I spend too much time on my phone.
I leave homework until the last minute.
I do not help much at home.

days.task:
Look at the 3 problems you wrote yesterday.
Think of one solution that could help improve all 3 problems.
days.example: If I follow a daily timetable for studying, phone use, and household work, all three problems could improve. The real problem is poor time management.

days.task:
Think about your 3 problems again.
How would your local role model handle them?
How would your global role model handle them?
Write both answers.
days.example:
Local role model (woman who runs a tiffin service) :
She would start working without waiting for motivation. She would take action, even if it was only for 10 minutes.
Global role model (APJ Abdul Kalam):
He believed in discipline and using time wisely. He would make a simple plan and follow it every day without needing others to remind him.

title: Challenge: Success Visualisation
rule: I will create a life that makes my family, friends, and society proud.

days.task:
Look at the 3 problems you found last week and the solution you chose.
Now break that solution into small daily actions that are easy to do every day.
days.example:
Example:
Problem: I waste time and forget my responsibilities.
Daily actions:
Every morning, I will write 3 tasks for the day.
I will not use social media until those tasks are finished.
Before sleeping, I will spend 15 minutes helping at home.
If I do not understand something in school, I will watch a YouTube video about it the same day.

days.task:
Share your problem and solution with people in your support group.
Ask for their suggestions and improve your plan.
days.example: My mother suggested keeping my phone in another room while studying. My teacher suggested using a notebook to track tasks. I added both ideas to my plan.

days.task:
Follow the suggestions from your support group.
At the end of the day, write:
What helped?
What did not help?
What will you do differently tomorrow?
days.example: Keeping my phone away helped me focus better. Writing a task list also helped. I forgot to help at home, so tomorrow I will set a reminder.

days.task:
Look back at everything you wrote and did during the last 4 weeks.
Answer these questions:
What did you believe about yourself in Week 1 that has changed now?
What is one new thing you learned about yourself?
Has the way you talk to yourself changed? Give one example.
What is one thing about your mindset that surprised you?
days.example: In Week 1, I thought my situation was stopping me from focusing. Now I realise my habits were the bigger problem. I also learned that I can solve problems when I stay calm. Before, I said, "I can't do this." Now I say, "I haven't figured this out yet."

days.task:
Think about everything you learned about yourself in the last 4 weeks - your strengths, natural talents, and interests.
What career would you like to choose, and how do you plan to reach it?
days.example: I think I want to work in public service as a teacher, government officer, or social worker. I am not fully sure yet, but this feels like the right direction.

days.task:
Write your personal success story in one sentence.
Imagine your life 10 years from now.
Include:
Your work
Your responsibilities
Your income
Do not overthink. Write the first honest answer that comes to your mind.
days.example: I have cleared the UPSC exam, I am working as a District Collector in my home state, helping my community, earning ₹80,000 per month, and my parents no longer worry about money.

title: Challenge: Practising to Build Confidence
rule: I will build confidence one small step at a time.

days.task:
Look at the success story you wrote in Week 4.
Now write 5 practical steps that can help you achieve that goal in the next 10 years.
days.example:
Focus on doing well in my board exams.
Learn more about the UPSC exam and syllabus.
Start reading a newspaper every day.
Find a mentor or someone who can guide me.
Improve my writing and communication skills.

days.task:
Look at your 5 steps.
Choose the easiest step that:
Costs no money
Needs no special preparation
Can be done today
This will be your first step towards your goal.
days.example: Watch a UPSC topper interview, read about the UPSC syllabus for 15 minutes, or talk to someone preparing for the exam.

days.task:
Do the easy step you chose yesterday for 15 minutes.
After finishing, write honestly how you felt.
days.example: I watched a UPSC topper interview. I learned that success comes from consistency, not being the smartest person. It made me feel that I can do it too.

days.task:
Do the same task again today, but spend 5 more minutes on it.
Then write how today felt compared to yesterday.
days.example: Yesterday I only watched an interview. Today I also wrote down 3 ideas that I can use in my own preparation.

days.task:
Talk to your support group about what you worked on this week.
Tell them about your goal and progress. Ask for suggestions and use at least one suggestion today.
days.example: My mother suggested that I study at the same time every day so it becomes a habit. I decided to follow that advice.

days.task:
Answer these 5 questions:
What improved this week, even a little?
What was easier than you expected?
What will you continue doing next week?
What new thing will you try next week?
What did you learn about yourself this week?
days.example:
I stopped waiting to feel ready and started taking action.
Taking the first step was easier than expected.
I will keep working on my goal for 15 minutes every day.
Next week I will talk to someone who is already on the same path.
I learned that I am more consistent than I thought.

title: Challenge: Understanding and Managing Your Fear
rule: I may feel fear, but I will not let it stop me.

days.task:
Write down the fears that stop you from taking action.
For each fear, answer:
What am I afraid will happen if I take action?
Honestly, how likely is it to happen?
days.example:
Fear: Speaking in class.
What I am afraid of:
People will laugh at me or think I said something wrong.
How likely is it?
Maybe 2 out of 10. Most people do not laugh when others speak.

days.task:
Choose one fear and break it into small steps.
First, set a weekly goal. Then choose one small task for today.
The task should feel a little uncomfortable but still possible.
days.example:
Fear: Speaking in class.
Weekly goal:
Speak at least once in every class this week.
Today's task:
Ask my doubt in class if I don't understand something.

days.task:
Face your fear by counting 3,2,1 and doing the small task immediately.
Keep going until you complete the task.
Then look at what you wrote on Day 1 and answer:
What actually happened?
days.example: I asked my question in class. The teacher answered normally. A few students had the same doubt. Nobody laughed. My fear was mostly in my imagination.

days.task:
Do one small thing today that is slightly harder than yesterday.
You can:
Ask for help
Share your opinion
Ask a question you have been holding back
days.example: Yesterday I asked a question after class. Today I answered a question in front of the class, even though I was not fully sure.

days.task:
Build confidence by practising every day.
For fear of speaking confidently, you can choose one activity:
-Speak in front of a mirror for 1 minute
-Talk to a family member or friend about a topic
-Say hello to someone new
-Ask your teacher a question
days.example: Today I spoke in front of a mirror for 1 minute about my future goals. I will continue doing this every day.

days.task:
Answer these questions honestly:
What did I do this week even though I was afraid?
What am I proud of about myself after this week?
What fear do I want to work on next week?
days.example:
This week I asked a question in front of the whole class, even though I was afraid.
I am proud that I did not let fear stop me. It may seem small, but it was a big step for me.
Next, I want to work on sharing my opinions more in group conversations.

title: Challenge: I Can Communicate
rule: I will listen, understand and then respond.

days.task:
Think honestly about how you communicate.
Choose one:
-I listen to understand the other person.
-I listen mainly to reply quickly.
If you reply quickly, try to understand your reaction. Why do you respond so fast?
If you listen to understand, notice whether a person's words and their real meaning are always the same.
days.example: I think I reply quickly because I feel uncomfortable with silence. I often focus on what I want to say next and miss what the other person is really saying.

days.task:
Ask people in your support group about your communication strengths and weaknesses.
Find out which of these you do well and which you need to improve:
Listen
Understand
Verify
Respond
days.example: My mother said I listen well when I am calm, but I interrupt when I disagree. I realised I usually listen and respond, but I often skip understanding and verifying.

days.task:
Choose one communication technique from the resource PDF that can help with your weakness.
Practice it in every conversation today.
days.example: I used "Repeat and Acknowledge." Before replying, I repeated what I understood. People often said, "Yes, exactly," which showed I was listening properly.

days.task:
Choose one communication technique from the resource PDF that can help with your weakness.
Practise it in every conversation today.
days.example: I used "Repeat and Acknowledge." Before replying, I repeated what I understood. People often said, "Yes, exactly," which showed I was listening properly.

days.task:
In a new conversation today, use any 2 communication techniques together.
Then write how the conversation went.
days.example: I used the "2-second pause" and "short, clear sentences." I paused before speaking and explained my thoughts more clearly than usual.

days.task:
Try to use all the communication techniques during the day in every conversation, big or small. Slowly you will see that this has become your natural way of expression and communication. 
At the end of the day, answer:
Which technique felt most natural?
Which technique was the hardest?
What is one moment when better communication helped you?
days.example: The "2-second pause" felt most natural. "Short, clear sentences" were still difficult. Better communication helped me explain my thoughts more clearly in a conversation.

title: Challenge: Mental Discipline
rule: I will show up every day and not give up.

days.task:
Write what you plan to do to keep building confidence, better communication and managing fear.
Create a simple timetable that includes:
Physical health
Mental health
Healthy food
Studies
Family time
Career goals
Personal development activities
days.example:
Morning (6:30-7:30 am)
Wake up, exercise for 15 minutes, eat breakfast
Study/Goal Time (4:00-6:00 pm)
School revision + 15 minutes for my career goal
Evening (8:00-9:00 pm)
Help at home, spend time with family, no phone after 9:00 pm

days.task:
Follow your timetable today as closely as possible.
At the end of the day, answer honestly:
-Did I follow my timetable today?
-What did I miss and why?
-What changes do I need to make?
Also write how do you plan to do your best to achieve your target and dream?
days.example: I followed most of my timetable. I missed my personal development task because I forgot. I will keep my timetable on my wall, desk, or phone wallpaper so I can see it during the day.

days.task:
Do something today for 15 minutes that is directly associated with your goal, target or vision at the exact same time you set in your timetable on Day 1 of this week.
No excuses. No delays.
Write what you did.
days.example: At 6:00 pm, I watched a video about UPSC preparation and wrote down 3 things I learned.

days.task:
Choose one difficult task or habit that you still struggle with.
Find what you can do to overcome it.
Trust yourself to do it and count 3,2,1 and start immediately.
After finishing, write about your experience.
days.example: I find it difficult to read the newspaper every day because it feels boring and hard to understand. Today, I pushed myself to read 5 short news stories on the Inshorts news app. It felt easier than I expected.

days.task:
Distraction is the enemy of discipline.
Make a list of your distractions.
For each one, write:
When it usually happens
What you will do instead
Avoid these distractions until you finish your daily targets.
You can also use Focus Mode on your phone.
days.example:
Distraction: Social media, shorts, or reels
When it happens: After school, before sleep, or when I am alone
What I will do instead: Keep my phone away until my work is finished and spend time on something useful.
Distraction: TV or OTT platforms
When it happens: When a task feels difficult or boring
What I will do instead: Take a short walk, do an easier task first, then return to the difficult task.

days.task:
Check how well you followed your timetable this week.
Reward yourself for the progress you made.
Then write your reflection:
How did I feel after being disciplined this week?
What did I learn about myself?
What will I continue next week?
days.example: I followed my timetable for the whole week. I proved to myself that I can be disciplined when I decide to be. I will continue following the same timetable next week.

title: Challenge: Fail to Grow
rule: I will not try to win. I will try to learn every day.

days.task:
Choose one skill that you are not good at right now.
It could be speaking English, solving maths problems, drawing, expressing yourself, confidence, eye contact, or anything else.
Answer these two questions honestly. Write your answers the way you think your local role model and global role model would answer them.
-Why am I not good at this right now?
-Why do I want to improve it?
days.example:
Skill: Speaking English confidently.
I am not good at it because I never practised speaking or learned by observing others, and I am afraid of making grammar mistakes in front of people.
I want to improve because most of the opportunities I want, like college interviews, job interviews, and talking to people outside my town, need confident English. If I do not improve, this will keep holding me back.

days.task:
Practise your chosen skill with one person from your support group.
Do not worry about making mistakes. Do not prepare too much. Just count 3,2,1 and start.
The goal is to experience failure in a safe environment with someone who supports you, lets you make mistakes, encourages you, and helps you improve.
days.example: I asked my older cousin to listen while I spoke in English for 3 minutes about my daily routine.

days.task:
Think about yesterday and answer these questions:
What went wrong?
Where did I struggle the most?
At what point did I feel like giving up?
Then ask the person from your support group for honest feedback.
Write what they noticed.
days.example: I lost confidence after making my first grammar mistake. My cousin said my vocabulary is actually good, but I panic too quickly.

days.task:
Choose only one mistake from yesterday. Practise improving only that one mistake for 15 minutes.
Do not try to fix every mistake at the same time. Then write your result.
days.example: I chose to stop quitting in the middle of a sentence after making a grammar mistake. I practiced speaking in front of a mirror for 15 minutes and made myself finish every sentence, even if it was not perfect.

days.task:
Practise the same skill again.
Then answer:
-What improved, even a little?
-What still feels difficult?
Now challenge yourself a little more. Speak for longer, try a slightly harder task, or add one new thing.
days.example:
My sentences were more complete than on Day 2. I still made mistakes, but I did not stop speaking.
What still feels difficult is finding the right words quickly. I still pause for too long.

days.task:
Answer these questions:
What did I fail at this week?
What did I learn from those failures?
What improved, even a little?
What will I do to become better next week?
days.example:
This week I failed at speaking smoothly and at a natural speed.
What I learned is that my biggest problem is not vocabulary or grammar. It is panic and self-doubt because I worry too much about being judged.
What improved is that I now finish my sentences instead of stopping halfway.

title: Challenge: Courage and Self-Trust
rule: I trust myself to take one step, no matter what happens.

days.task:
Continue doing the one task you planned for your self-development.
Do not set a new goal today. Just keep the promise you made to yourself and practise being consistent.
days.example: I continued my 15 minutes of English speaking practice today, just like I planned in Week 9.

days.task:
Write down all the small problems, difficulties, or habits that you have been avoiding, ignoring, or postponing while working towards your goal.
Be completely honest.
days.example:
-I am not practising every day.
-I am not reading the news to improve my knowledge and vocabulary.
-I doubt myself.
-I am not serious about my goal.
-I worry too much about what others think.
-I lose focus.
-I overthink, so I avoid or delay my work.

days.task:
Look at the problems you wrote yesterday.
For each problem:
-Find one simple solution.
-If you cannot find one, ask your support group for help.
-If you are still unsure, think about what your local or global role model would do. Then make that your own solution.
days.example:
Problem 1: I am not serious about my goal.
Cause: I get distracted by social media or my own thoughts.
Solution: I will remind myself that reaching this goal can improve my future, so I will make it a priority.
Problem 2: I judge myself too harshly.
Cause: I compare myself with people who are much better than me.
Solution: I will remember that success takes time, just like a mango tree or a bamboo tree needs time to grow.

days.task:
Trust yourself and use your solutions today.
Try to do them at least 3 times.
Then write how your mindset and confidence changed.
Write both your positive and negative feelings honestly.
days.example:
I practised speaking English three times today; morning, afternoon, and evening.
What changed in my mindset: A week ago, I was doing this once a day just to say, "I did it". Today I did it three times because I actually want to get better.

days.task:
Ask yourself: Am I ready to level up? If yes, write your next goal. What is the next level of this skill or goal that you want to work on?
If no, answer honestly:
-What is stopping me?
-Can I solve that problem before next week?
days.example:
Yes. I am ready to level up.
My next goal is to have one English conversation with someone I do not know well, like a classmate or a teacher.

days.task:
After completing these first 10 weeks of the course, write down the things you can now trust yourself to do.
Be specific.
days.example:
-I can practise for 15 minutes even when I do not feel like it.
-I can face my fears instead of running away.
-I now try first instead of assuming I will fail.
-I have a strong support group that I can ask for help when I need it.
-I do not give up easily.
-I understand that good things take time.

title: Challenge: Building Resilience Nature's Way
rule: I may bend, I may slow down, but I will not stop

days.task:
Spend 5 minutes looking at a plant or tree nearby. Notice that it looks still, but it is growing every day.
If you cannot find a plant, close your eyes and imagine a seed growing into a tree.
Then answer these questions honestly:
-Where do I feel stuck in my life right now?
-Am I expecting quick results, like trying to break the rock on the first hit?
-What is one small action I can repeat every day to slowly overcome this problem?
days.example:
Where I feel stuck: My English speaking is improving, but very slowly.
Yes. I think I expect to become fluent in just a few weeks.
One small daily action: Read an article aloud for 15 minutes every day, even if I make mistakes.

days.task:
Spend 15 minutes doing something difficult that helps you move towards your goal.
Write what happened.
If you see no result or progress today, that is okay.
Stay calm under pressure like water. Adapt instead of giving up.
days.example: I practised speaking in English about a news article. I stopped many times because I did not like how I sounded. On my fourth try, I decided to keep speaking without stopping.

days.task:
Repeat the same task for the next 2 days.
Do not focus on getting results. Focus on staying committed for 15 minutes every day.
Notice any changes in:
Your mindset
Your approach
Your beliefs
Write your observations.
Keep doing the boring but important work; practice, revision, and repetition. Do not complain. Learn to overcome challenges.
days.example: I did the same task again today. I did not see a big improvement, but I still completed my 15 minutes. Earlier, I would get frustrated when I did not see immediate results. This time, I stayed patient and focused on finishing the task.

days.task:
Repeat the same task for the next 2 days.
Do not focus on getting results. Focus on staying committed for 15 minutes every day.
Notice any changes in:
Your mindset
Your approach
Your beliefs
Write your observations.
Keep doing the boring but important work; practice, revision, and repetition. Do not complain. Learn to overcome challenges.
days.example: I did the same task again today. I did not see a big improvement, but I still completed my 15 minutes. Earlier, I would get frustrated when I did not see immediate results. This time, I stayed patient and focused on finishing the task.

days.task:
Do your usual task today, but push yourself a little more.
For example:
Practise for 2 extra minutes.
Solve 2 more questions.
Do 2 more minutes of mirror talk.
Make one more attempt.
Then write how you felt.
days.example: I added 2 extra minutes to my speaking practice and spoke in front of my family for the first time. It felt difficult, but I think this is how real growth begins.

days.task:
Answer these questions:
What are 3 moments this week when I did not give up?
What are 2 times I handled a difficult situation better than before?
What is 1 thing that improved slowly, even if only a little?
Remember, you grow by continuing even when things are hard.
days.example:
3 moments I did not give up:
On Day 2, I kept trying after failing several times.
On Day 3, I continued even though I saw no results.
On Day 5, I practised longer even when I was tired.
2 times I handled difficulty better:
On Day 4, I usually stop when I don't like how I sound. This time I kept speaking.
On Day 5, I saw no progress and wanted to quit. I finished my 15 minutes anyway.

title: Challenge: The Smart Risk-Taker Mindset
rule: I will not wait until I feel ready. I will become ready by trying every day

days.task:
Think about the person you want to become.
-What steps do you need to take to become that person?
-What risks do you need to take to reach your goal?
-Write your answers and this week's action.
days.example:
One risk I have been avoiding:
Telling my parents about the career I want because I am afraid they may not support me.
This week's action:
I will have an honest, open, and respectful conversation with my parents. I will explain my research, my plan, and my goals to help them understand and reduce their worries.

days.task:
Before taking the risk, answer these 3 questions with as much detail as you can:
Best case: What is the best thing that could happen?
Worst case: What is the worst thing that could happen?
Most likely: What do I think will actually happen?
days.example:
Best case: My parents listen, understand, and support my choice.
Worst case: They get upset and say no.
Most likely: They may have concerns, but they will listen if I explain my plan calmly, clearly, and confidently.

days.task:
Ask yourself honestly:
How ready am I to take this risk? (Out of 100)
If your answer is 60 or above, count 3,2,1 and take the first step.
If your answer is below 60, write what would help you feel more ready.
Then ask yourself:
Can I do that today?
Am I waiting for more preparation, or am I waiting for the courage that only comes after taking action?
days.example: My readiness is 65 out of 100. I feel nervous, but I am ready enough to have the conversation today.

days.task:
Write honestly about what happened after you took the risk.
Answer these questions:
Did it go well or not so well?
What did I learn from this experience?
How will I improve and move forward?
days.example:
It did not go completely well. My father supported me, but my mother was worried about job security. I became defensive, and the conversation became tense.
I learned that I explained my plan well, but I also needed to understand my mother's concerns 
Next time, I will let my mother share all her concerns, listen carefully, and reassure her calmly before explaining my plan again.

days.task:
Take the same risk again, but this time use what you learned on Day 4.
It does not have to be perfect. It only needs to be better than your first attempt.
Then write:
What fear did I overcome today?
days.example: I overcame the fear that my parents' worries meant they did not believe in me. I realised they worry because they care about me, not because they doubt me.

days.task:
Answer these questions honestly.
This week:
What did I learn about myself this week?
What fear did I overcome?
How did I overcome it?
Last 4 weeks:
What did I learn about my mindset during the last 4 weeks of Phase 3?
days.example:
I learned that I used to avoid difficult situations until I felt completely ready. Now I understand that confidence and readiness come from trying consistently, not from waiting.
The fear I overcame was telling my parents about the career I want. 
I overcame it by preparing my plan properly, accepting that the worst case was survivable, and then having the conversation.

title: Challenge: Train Your Mind to Grow
rule: I am improving, not just proving.

days.task:
Read your answers and reflections from the last 12 weeks.
Then answer honestly:
Based on your actions so far, are you:
An organic farmer (patient, consistent, focused on long-term growth),
A chemical farmer (looking for shortcuts, inconsistent, focused on quick results),
or somewhere in between?
Write your answer and give examples from your own behaviour.
days.example: I think I am mostly an organic farmer. I have practised consistently for the last 3 weeks. I no longer avoid difficult tasks, and I have started facing my challenges instead of running away from them.

days.task:
Write 5 things you cannot do, struggle with, or have not tried yet.
Write each one like this: "I can't ______ yet."
Read them again and think about the possibilities.
Then choose one and answer:
What do I need to do to change my "yet" into "now"?
days.example:
Before:
I can't speak English confidently in front of strangers.
I can't spend a whole day without checking my phone every 30 minutes.
After:
I can't speak English confidently in front of strangers yet. But now I have started speaking confidently with my support group and family, so I know I can keep improving.

days.task:
Choose one task from yesterday's list.
Work on it for 15 minutes today.
The goal is not to be perfect. The goal is to give your best effort.
Then answer:
What effort did I make today?
Did my effort improve the result, even a little?
days.example:
Task: Studying a subject I usually avoid because it feels difficult.
My effort: Instead of only reading, I wrote down every concept I did not understand and researched for the answers before moving on.
Improvement: I got through fewer pages than usual, but I actually understood what I read.

days.task:
Do the same task as Day 3 again today.
This time, use a different method, not just more effort.
Write:
What new method did I use?
What happened?
days.example:
New method:
Instead of studying alone, I explained the topic to my younger sibling as if I were the teacher.
Outcome:
I realised which concepts I truly understood and which ones I still needed to learn.

days.task:
Think about your local role model and global role model.
How would each of them do the same task you have been practising this week?
Try one of their approaches today.
Then write what happened.
days.example:
My global role model: APJ Abdul Kalam.
His approach:
He would not wait for perfect conditions. So I studied as if I had an exam tomorrow, with full focus, discipline and commitment.

days.task:
Answer these questions:
What are 3 things I improved this week?
What are 2 mistakes I learned from?
What is 1 challenge I handled better than before?
days.example:
3 things I improved:
I tried different ways instead of repeating the same method.
I studied actively instead of only reading.
I did not quit when the task became difficult.
2 mistakes I learned from:
I realised I was sometimes looking for quick results instead of being patient.
I found that I did not understand some topics as well as I thought.
1 challenge I handled better:
I stopped saying "I can't" and started saying "I can't...yet." This helped me think more positively and keep trying.

title: Challenge: Let Go to Grow
rule: I let go of what holds me back and make room for what moves me forward.

days.task:
Think about your preferred activity.
Write the 3 best things you have learned or improved in it so far.
days.example:
Preferred activity: Communication
I make eye contact while speaking.
I pause before I respond instead of reacting immediately.
I take small steps to start conversations.

days.task:
Think about your goal.
Write 3 beliefs that are stopping you from improving or achieving your goal.
Write them exactly as they sound in your mind.
days.example:
Belief 1: I do not know enough to speak confidently.
Belief 2: I mix up my words and embarrass myself.
Belief 3: I can never communicate as well as the confident people in my class.

days.task:
Take each belief from Day 2 and change it into a positive, action-based statement.
Whenever the old belief comes back, notice it and read your new statement. The more you do this, the weaker the old belief becomes.
days.example:
Old thought: "I mix up my words and embarrass myself."
New thought: "Making mistakes means I am learning. I will keep going even when I stumble."

days.task:
Think about one habit or thought that stops you from believing in yourself.
Choose one small thing to stop doing today.
Then write what you will do instead when that habit or thought comes back.
days.example:
Habit that is not helping me: Re-reading my old notes over and over before practising because I never feel fully prepared.
What I will do instead: I will trust the practice I have already done. I will not doubt my hard work.

days.task:
Spend 15 minutes practising your skill in a new way.
Use a different method than you normally do to improve your skill and build confidence.
days.example:
What I usually do:
I read articles and make notes before I practise speaking.
New method:
Today I watched two short YouTube videos about my topic. Then I spoke about the topic for 10 minutes without using notes or any other help.

days.task:
Answer these questions:
1 thing I learned this week.
1 thing I unlearned this week.
1 thing I relearned in a new way.
days.example:
I learned: Small changes in the way I practice can make a big difference.
I unlearned: The belief that I do not have to be perfect before I take action.
I relearned: Consistent practice helps me improve, even when I do not see quick results.

title: Challenge: Work Hard + Work Smart
rule: I will work hard with the right plan and stay disciplined.

days.task:
What is the one skill you want to become really good at?
If possible, choose something that matches your natural talent.
Write:
What is the skill?
Why do you want to master it?
days.example:
The skill: Teaching and explaining complex things in a way anyone can understand.
Why: People have always told me I explain things clearly and simply so I want to master this skill fully.

days.task:
Write 3 things that are making it difficult for you to reach your goal.
Be honest.
days.example:
My practice method has not improved.
I stay in my comfort zone instead of trying difficult tasks.
I compare myself with others and lose confidence.

days.task:
Write 3 specific things you need to improve, correct, or build to perform your best.
Be as specific as possible.
days.example:
I need to practice more difficult topics instead of only easy ones.
I need to track my daily practise and learn from my mistakes.
I need to stop waiting to feel motivated. I will count 3,2,1 and start.

days.task: Write 3 ways you will avoid distractions while working on your goal.
days.example:
I will keep my phone in another room before I start working.
I will turn on Focus Mode or Do Not Disturb while I study.
I will finish my daily target before using social media or watching TV.

days.task:
Today, follow your plan.
Work on your goal with the right focus, method and mindset.
Then answer:
What did I complete today?
How well did I do it?
Did I work smart?
days.example:
I studied for 20 minutes and explained the topic out loud instead of only reading it.
It went better than my usual sessions, because explaining it out loud showed me which parts I actually understood. 
I think I did work smart. The new method helped me learn the topic more clearly.

days.task:
Think about how you worked this week.
Ask yourself:
Is there a faster, smarter, or better way to do the same task?
Write your answer.
days.example: A better way I found: Instead of practising alone every day, I can record myself once a week and watch it to find areas where I can improve.

title: Challenge: Understand Natural Hints
rule: I will watch closely. Everything around me has something to teach.

days.task:
Find a quiet place, such as your balcony, window, room, or somewhere outside.
Sit quietly for 5 minutes without your phone.
Observe everything around you:
Sounds, Movement, People, Wind, Birds, Light
Then write:
3 things you noticed that you had never noticed before.
What gives you energy?
What drains your energy?
days.example:
3 things I noticed:
Nature follows a routine. It begins the day in the morning and rests by evening.
The wind is always there, but sometimes it is strong and sometimes it is gentle.
Many people seem busy all the time and spend very little time in nature.
What gives me energy:
Starting my day with a plan, finishing my daily tasks and having meaningful conversations.
What drains my energy:
Overthinking, self-doubt, and comparing myself with others.

days.task:
Think about one important situation in your life that matters to you.
Try to understand why it happened.
Look at the situation from both sides, understand the other person's point of view (if there is one), and stay neutral.
Then ask yourself:
What good could come from this situation in the future?
days.example:
Situation:
I practiSed my skill for three days, but I do not feel I have improved.
My side:
I feel frustrated because I worked hard but cannot see results.
Other side:
Three days is not enough time to see big changes.
What good could come from this:
I have learned that I need more patience and consistent practice.

days.task:
Observe or imagine a tree on a windy day.
The tree bends with the wind, but it does not break.
It does not fight the wind. It moves with it while staying strong.
Then write:
What does the tree teach you?
What is one situation today where you can be flexible instead of being stubborn or resistant?
days.example:
What the tree teaches me:
I can change my approach without giving up on my goal.
One situation today:
I will listen to my support group and be open to trying new ideas and methods.

days.task:
In one conversation today, practise being an observer and a good listener.
Pay attention to:
The person's tone
Their emotions
What they really mean, not just their words
If possible, use the Listen → Understand → Verify → Respond technique from Week 7.
After the conversation, write one new thing you understood about that person.
days.example: I listened to my friend talk about his exam stress without interrupting. I realised he did not want advice - he just wanted someone to listen.

days.task:
Answer these questions honestly:
When do I get distracted the most?
When do I perform my best?
What pattern do I notice in my failures or struggles?
Then ask yourself:
What is this pattern trying to teach me?
days.example:
When I get distracted:
When a task feels difficult or I cannot see immediate results.
When I perform my best:
When I have a fixed time and one clear goal.
My pattern:
I keep checking my phone instead of staying focused.
What it is teaching me:
I need to control distractions and stay focused on one task at a time.

days.task:
Answer these questions:
What are 3 things I observed this week that taught me something?
What is 1 pattern that has been holding me back?
What is 1 decision I made this week because of what I learned?
days.example:
3 things I observed:
Nature taught me not to rush.
I learned that people sometimes only want someone to listen.
The tree taught me to stay flexible while moving towards my goal.
1 pattern holding me back:
I start with excitement but lose consistency after a few days.
1 decision I made:
I have decided to observe more, stay open to learning and look for lessons in everyday life.

title: Challenge: Understanding and Managing Stress
rule: I notice stress early and respond calmly.

days.task:
Think about the last time you felt stressed.
Write a few lines about what happened.
Then answer:
Was it good stress that helped you grow, or bad stress that made you feel overwhelmed?
What happens to your mind or body when you feel stressed? (For example: headache, fast heartbeat, fast breathing, overthinking, worry, fear, feeling numb, irritation, anger, or getting distracted.)
days.example:
Situation:
My exam results came out, and I scored lower than I expected.
Type of stress:
It was bad stress. It did not motivate me. It made me feel like I was not good enough.
How I felt:
I felt disappointed, lost, and demotivated.

days.task:
Choose one situation that causes you stress (for example: exams, pressure, comparison, competition, or anything else).
Find the real reason behind your stress.
Think about it yourself first. If you are not sure, ask your support group for their opinion.
days.example: I feel stressed when I compare my progress with others. I know everyone has a different journey, but I forget that whenever I see someone doing better than me.

days.task:
Choose one stressful situation.
Break it into small, simple steps to make it easier to manage.
Remember, when a problem feels too big, focus only on the next step, not the whole problem.
Accept good stress because it helps you build self-control.
days.example:
Stressful situation:
Class presentation in 5 days.
My steps:
Choose my topic today, research it, and make notes.
Practise my presentation alone at least two times using the communication techniques I have learned.
Present it to one family member or someone from my support group and ask for feedback.
Improve my presentation using their feedback and practise again.
Do one final practice on Day 5 and present it in class.

days.task:
Try this small exercise. Sit quietly for 5 minutes without using any technology. Relax your body and control your breathing.
Breathe in for 4 seconds and breathe out for 6 seconds.
A longer exhale tells your body that it is safe and helps you feel calmer.
After 5 minutes, write how you felt compared to before.
days.example:
Before:
My mind was jumping from one worry to another.
After 5 minutes:
My problems were still there, but I felt much calmer and more in control.

days.task:
Do 10-15 minutes of physical activity today.
You can go for a walk, stretch, or do light exercise.
Then write how you felt afterwards.
days.example: I felt lighter and more relaxed. I did not realise how tense my body was until I started moving.

days.task:
The next time you feel stressed, talk to someone in your support group.
Ask them to listen without interrupting or giving advice.
Then create your own stress-management plan.
Write:
2 ways you can manage stress.
Which method worked best for you this week?
days.example:
Stress talk:
I told my mother I was feeling overwhelmed and asked her to just listen. Saying it out loud made me feel much better.
2 ways I can manage stress:
Remind myself that stress will pass, just like day and night or waves in the sea.
Prepare early by thinking about possible problems and planning simple solutions.
What worked best this week:
Talking to someone and taking slow, deep breaths helped me calm down the most.

title: Challenge: Build Emotional Intelligence
rule: I notice, understand and respond - I do not react.

days.task:
Sit quietly for 5 minutes without your phone.
Close your eyes and imagine your thoughts and emotions as clouds passing through the sky.
Then answer:
What emotion did you notice?
Did the feeling stay the whole time, or did it change?
days.example:
Emotion I noticed: Anxiety.
It was strong at first, but after a few minutes it became less intense and easier to manage.

days.task:
Observe one person today who seems stressed, worried, distracted, or upset.
Do not interrupt or interfere. Just observe.
Then answer:
How do you think they are feeling?
Why might they be feeling that way?
If you were in the same situation, what would you do?
days.example:
The person I observed:
My friend during our study session.
How they seemed:
He looked distracted and kept staring at his book without reading.
Why he might feel that way:
He may have felt overwhelmed because there was too much to study.
What I would do:
I would stay calm, use the self-control techniques I have learned, and focus on one task at a time.

days.task:
Look at yourself in a mirror when you feel stressed, worried, or upset.
Ask yourself:
How am I feeling today?
Why do I feel this way?
Then choose one way to help yourself feel better, such as journaling, talking to someone, accepting your feelings, or letting them go.
days.example:
I feel low today because I worked hard this week but still feel it was not enough.
I wrote about the good things I achieved in my journal, and I felt a little better afterwards.

days.task:
Pause during 3 emotional moments today.
Each time, ask yourself:
What am I feeling right now?
Why am I feeling this way?
Write your answers.
days.example:
I feel proud because I completed my daily practice even though I wanted to delay it.
I feel frustrated because my brother interrupted me twice while I was studying.

days.task: Write 3 routines, habits, or patterns that help you stay calm, focused, balanced and in control during the day.
days.example:
I follow my morning routine before checking my phone.
I finish my most important task before doing anything else.
I take short breaks when I start feeling stressed or distracted.

days.task:
Notice 5 emotional moments today, whether they are big or small, positive or negative.
Write each one like this:
"I feel ___ because ___."
Do not write "I am ___."
"I feel" describes a temporary emotion that will pass. "I am" makes it part of your identity.
days.example:
I feel grateful because my friend checked on me today.
I feel irritated because I wasted an hour scrolling on my phone without noticing.

title: Challenge: Become Adaptable
rule: I learn, I adjust and I move forward.

days.task:
Think about how COVID changed your life and your family.
Write:
What changed?
How did you and your family deal with those changes?
What is one way your family adapted during that time?
days.example:
Note: 
There is no right or wrong answer. Write what is true for you and what feels like you.

days.task:
Think about 3 things you have known for a long time that you needed to improve, change, or learn, but never did.
For each one, write why you did not change or what stopped you.
days.example:
1st thing I need to change: I know I should spend less time on social media. I keep saying, "I'll start from Monday."I've not changed this habit of mine yet because change feels harder than continuing.
2nd thing I need to change: I know I should ask questions when I do not understand something in class. I never do it because it would make me look slow learner.

days.task:
Choose one thing from yesterday's list.
Spend 15 minutes trying a new way to improve it. Make it your priority today. Do not postpone it.
days.example: My commitment is that at 5pm today I will read one article related to my field for 15 minutes - no phone, no interruptions.

days.task:
Think of one situation today that did not go as planned, big or small.
Instead of reacting with frustration, pause and ask yourself:
"What can I do now?"
Then write:
What happened?
How did you respond?
days.example: I planned to study after school, but some relatives came home unexpectedly. I felt frustrated and wasted almost an hour before deciding to study later in the evening. I still completed my work, but I realised I could have adjusted sooner instead of wasting time.

days.task:
Talk to someone from your support group about the situation from Day 4.
Tell them what happened and how you handled it. Ask them what they think you could do differently if a similar situation happens again.
Listen carefully without arguing or becoming defensive.
Write:
What suggestion did they give you?
How will you use it next time?
days.example: I told my mother that I wasted an hour because I was upset my study plan had changed. She suggested that whenever something unexpected happens, I should quickly make a new plan instead of waiting for things to become normal. Next time, I will adjust my schedule immediately and continue with my work.

days.task:
Choose one situation you have been avoiding because it feels uncomfortable.
Instead of avoiding it, do it today.
Then answer:
What did you adapt to?
Which adaptation technique did you use?
Colour change - understanding the situation and adjusting.
Ink release - creating space to think before acting.
Body squeezing - finding a new way around the problem.
How did it feel?
days.example:
I shared my opinion during a group discussion instead of staying quiet.
Adaptation technique:
Colour change. I understood the situation and adjusted instead of staying silent.
How it felt:
It felt uncomfortable at first, but after a few seconds I became more confident and people listened to me.

title: Challenge: Building Consistency
rule: No matter what, I show up every day.

days.task:
Think about the situations when you feel like giving up or skipping your commitment.
Write them down honestly.
Think about things like:
Feeling lazy or tired, Getting distracted, Negative thoughts, Poor results, Family or personal problems, Festivals or social events, Losing support, Feeling satisfied with past success
days.example:
When I wake up and don't feel motivated.
When my practice does not go well.
During festivals when my daily routine breaks.

days.task:
Think about why you want to stay consistent with your goal, no matter what happens.
Write the real reasons that will help you keep going.
days.example: My genuine reason is that I have already completed 20 weeks. If I stop now, all my hard work will go to waste.

days.task:
Choose one activity that you will do every day for the next week.
It can be related to your studies, fitness, mental health, reducing phone use, or anything connected to your goal.
Write:
What you will do
What time you will do it
How long you will do it
Do it for at least 15 minutes every day.
days.example:
What I will do: Practise Maths by solving questions.
Time: 6:00 pm every day.
Duration: 30 minutes.

days.task:
Do your minimum 15-minute commitment today, even if something unexpected happens.
Do not skip it or postpone it.
After you finish, write:
Did you complete it?
How did you feel after doing it?
days.example:
I completed more than 15 minutes even though I was tired.
After finishing, I felt proud because I kept my promise to myself.

days.task:
Look back at your journey.
Read your Week 1 answers, your Week 4 success story, and your reflections from each phase.
Then write:
How have you changed since Week 1?
What improvements do you notice?
days.example:
In Week 1, I used to overthink and delay everything.
Now I use the 3,2,1 rule and start without thinking too much.
I also observe situations more carefully before reacting.

days.task:
The sun rises every day without waiting for motivation or perfect conditions. It simply does its duty.
Think about your own life and future.
Write:
What will be your daily duty towards your life and career?
What will you do every day, no matter what happens?
Why is it important for your future?
days.example:
My daily duty is to improve myself every day.
No matter how I feel, I will study for at least 30 minutes and spend 15 minutes building the skills needed for my dream career.
I know that small daily efforts will help me achieve my long-term goals, so I will keep showing up every day.

title: Challenge: Design Your Career Roadmap
rule: I don't need perfect answers. I just need a direction.

days.task:
Think about yourself and answer these questions.
What are 3 things you enjoy doing?
What are 3 things you are good at?
What are 2 things people often praise you for?
What is 1 thing you have loved since childhood?
days.example:
I enjoy reading, drawing, and playing cricket.
I am good at explaining things, planning and solving puzzles.
People praise me for being kind and helpful.
I have loved cricket since I was little.

days.task:
Look at your answers from Day 1. Choose 3 careers that match your interests, strengths and personality.
Do not choose a career because someone else wants you to. Choose careers that feel right for you.
For each career, write: Why does this career suit you?
Next, find 2 other careers that are similar to your favourite career.
For each one, write:
What does this person do every day?
Why does this career interest you?
days.example:
My Top 3 Careers
Sports Coach: I enjoy cricket and I like teaching others.
Sports Journalist: I enjoy writing and talking about sports.
Sports Manager: I like planning and organising events.
Related Careers: Cricket Umpire and Sports Teacher

days.task:
Choose one career from your list. Now find one real person who is successful in that career.
Write these answers:
-What do they do?
-What qualities helped them succeed?
-What can you learn from them?
days.example:
Career: Cricket Coach
Person: Rahul Dravid
He trains young cricketers and helps them improve their skills.
He is patient, disciplined, hardworking, and calm.
What I can learn from him is that you do not have to be the most talented person to succeed.

days.task:
Look at your strengths, interests and personality. Now think about all the careers you explored. Which one career matches you the best?
Write 2 or 3 reasons why you think it is the best match for you.
days.example:
The career that matches me best is Sports Coach. Because I enjoy teaching others, 
I stay calm when problems happen and I like sports and want to help players improve.

days.task:
Yesterday, you chose the career that fits you best. Today, think about what you need to do to succeed in that career.
Answer these questions:
-Why is this career the right choice for me?
-Do I have the qualities this career needs?
-What skills do I already have?
-What new subjects or skills do I need to learn?
-What habits will help me succeed in this career?
days.example:
Career: Sports Coach
-This career is right for me because I enjoy teaching and helping others.
-I need to learn more about coaching and sports science.
-I need to practise every day, stay disciplined, and keep learning.

days.task:
You have spent the whole week learning about yourself and your career.
Now it is time to make your plan.
Answer these questions:
1.Which career do I want to explore with my full effort?
2. What is my Plan A to reach this career?
3. If Plan A does not work, what is my Plan B?
4. Why will I keep working towards this career, even when it feels difficult?
days.example:
Career: Sports Coach
Plan A: I will learn more about sports, join a coaching course, and practise coaching.
Plan B: I will become a sports teacher and continue learning about coaching.
I will I keep going because I enjoy helping others improve, and I want to build my future in sports.

title: Challenge: Build Your 5-Year Growth Plan
rule: Big dreams come true when I take small steps every day.

days.task:
Close your eyes and imagine your life 5 years from today.
Think about one normal day in your future.
Now answer these questions:
-Where am I? (Which city, school, college, or workplace?)
-What am I doing on a normal day?
-What skills do I have that I am learning today?
days.example: I am studying at a sports management college in Pune. Every day I attend classes, learn from my teachers and practise coaching. I have strong communication, leadership and teamwork skills because I started building them 5 years ago.

days.task:
Yesterday, you imagined where you want to be in 5 years.
Today, break that dream into smaller goals.
Answer these questions:
-What do I want to achieve by the end of Year 1?
-What do I want to achieve by the end of Year 3?
-What do I want to achieve by the end of Year 5?
Make each goal clear and specific.
days.example:
Year 1: I will improve my communication skills and score good marks in school.
Year 3: I will get into a college that matches my career goal.
Year 5: I will complete my degree and gain real work experience.

days.task:
Yesterday, you wrote the goals you want to achieve. Today, learn from people who have already achieved similar goals.
Think about your role models (global or local) and answer these questions:
-What skills or qualities helped them succeed?
-Which 3 of those skills do I want to start building today?
days.example: I need to develop good communication skills, mental toughness and learn to stay consistent even when results are slow or things get difficult.

days.task:
Your skills grow through your daily habits.
Choose 2 habits that will help you reach your Year 1 Goal.
Try to follow them every day for the rest of the week.
days.example:
Habit 1: I will study or practise for 15 minutes every day after school.
Habit 2: I will read or watch something about my career for 10 minutes every morning.

days.task:
Every goal has challenges.
Think about 2 challenges that might stop you from reaching your Year 1 Goal.
Then write how you will deal with each one.
days.example:
Challenge: I may get distracted.
My Plan: I will study in a quiet place and keep my phone in another room.

days.task:
You have made your plan.
Now think about how you will keep going, even when things become difficult.
Answer these questions:
-What will I do if I feel like giving up?
-How will I stay focused on my Year 1 Goal?
Write one promise to yourself that you will follow.
days.example:
If I feel like giving up I will take one small step instead of stopping.
I will stay focused by following my daily habits and asking for help when I need it.

title: Challenge: Become the Eagle
rule: I do not wait to feel ready. I trust myself and fly.

days.task:
You have spent 23 weeks learning and growing.
Now think about yourself.
-What is one positive change you have seen in yourself since you started this course?
-How did this change happen?
days.example:
Positive Change: I no longer wait for the perfect time to start.
How it happened: I completed small tasks every day, and that helped me become more confident.

days.task:
Think about your Year 1 Goal.
-What fear, self-doubt, or comfort zone is still holding you back?
-Why does it stop you?
Now take one small step today to overcome it.
Finally, write:
What happened when I took that step?
days.example:
I am afraid of making mistakes. It stops me because I worry that people will judge me for getting something wrong.

Today I asked a question in class even though I was not sure it was a good one. Nobody reacted the way I feared, and my teacher actually said it was a useful question.

days.task:
Today, do something you would normally avoid because of fear or self-doubt.
Make the decision by yourself.
Afterwards, reflect on your experience. Write about the decision you made, why you chose it, and how it will help you become more confident.
days.example: I asked my teacher for extra speaking practice, which I normally avoid because I do not like drawing attention to myself. I chose it because speaking confidently is the skill I want to master.

days.task:
Today, complete your Year 1 development task in a different way.
Do not worry about the final result.
Just give your best effort and finish the task.
After you finish, write about what happened, what went well, and one thing you want to improve next time.
days.example:
